title: Bananas (per lb)

drivers.name: Store closed Monday
drivers.evidence: One day closure in a 7-day week reduces capacity by ~14.3%. No past closure data; effect is estimated from typical day-weighted sales. Baseline assumes 7-day sales; actual sales likely 6/7 of that.

drivers.name: Price increase (1.5%)
drivers.evidence: Recent sales at $0.68 show no lift (524 and 388 units). A 1.5% price hike likely suppresses demand slightly; noise-adjusted estimate from similar past price changes suggests -1% to -2%.

adjustment.analysis: The target week has no events, but the store is closed Monday, reducing the selling days. The price increase to $0.68 (+1.5%) is small and not a promotion. Recent weeks show no price lift effect: at $0.68, sales were 524 (2026-09-28) and 388 (2026-10-05), both near baseline. The baseline already reflects a downward trend (trend_13_vs_prior_13_pct = -12.2%) and seasonal lull after back-to-school. The Thanksgiving uplift model (x1.37) is irrelevant here—no Thanksgiving event is near. A store closure on Monday reduces expected sales, but no historical closure data exists. The median multiplier must reflect reduced days and a small price hike. Evidence is thin, so shrink toward 1.0. The 5%-95% range remains unchanged unless a driver introduces uncertainty.

brief:
PRODUCT: Bananas (per lb) | category Produce | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-22 (6 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 0.68 (+1.5% vs regular price 0.67)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 438.2 | 5%-95%: 312.4 - 556.2 | 10%-90%: 346.4 - 529.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-21% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
